case_name: Dukhmochan Pandey v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

25 September 1997
Cr.A. No. 197 with Cr.A. No. 198 of 1982
The Judgment was delivered by: G. B. Pattanaik, J.
1. Both these appeals arise out of one sessions trial, Sessions Trial No. 125 of 1975 which was disposed of by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Darbhanga on 30th March, 1978. By the said judgment the accused persons were convicted under Section 302/149 and were sentenced to imprisonment for life. Twenty seven of the accused persons were convicted u/s. 147 but no separate sentence was awarded. Rest of the accused persons were convicted u/s. 147 but no separate sentence was awarded. Rest of the accused persons were convicted u/s. 148 IPC but no separate sentence was awarded. Accused Dukhmochan pandey, Sarbnarain Mishra, Upendra Pandey, Sanjam Pandey, Jainandan Mishra, Kapileshwar Mandal, Bhuvneshwar Mandal, Janak Das, Uttam Pandey, Tapeshwar Pandey, kameshwar Pandey and Jiwachh Mishra were convicted under Section 30
facts: Both these appeals arise out of one sessions trial, Sessions Trial No. 125 of 1975 which was disposed of by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Darbhanga on 30th March, 1978.
A dispute arose when informant Kapileshwar Pandey sent labourers to his field for transplanting paddy seeds.
On 25.7.1974 during morning hours while labourers of Kapileshwar Pandey numbering about 20 were transplanting paddy seeds on the field and asked the labourers to stop their work.
Kapileshwar Pandey, PW-18 objected to such high handed action of the mob whereupon accused Uttam Pandey and Upendra Pandey directed the mob to kill the labourers.
Soon thereafter accused Dukhmochan Pandey and Sarbnarain Mishra fired from their respective guns as a result of which Razaullah and Ahmed Shah, who were on the field fell down.
issues: Whether the prosecution has been able to prove the charges against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
Whether the conviction under Section 302/149 can be upheld.
Whether the object of the unlawful assembly being to stop the laborers from transplanting paddy seeds on the field in question, the conviction under Section 302/149 cannot be upheld.
petitioner_arguments: The star witness of the prosecution is Kapileshwar Pandey, PW-18 and his evidence is unbelievable and shaky and could not be relied upon.

The other eye-witnesses have merely repeated the incident in a parrot like manner and the very fact that each of them have mentioned the name of the accused persons in the same chronology is enough to hold that they are the tutored witnesses and as such no reliance can be placed on them.

If two of the appellants had gun with them and both of them simultaneously fired the gun as stated by the prosecution witnesses but they have not been able to indicate as to whose gun shot hit which deceased, the conviction of these appellants dividing in two groups and making each member responsible for death of one of the deceased is wholly unsustainable.

The delayed examination of the prosecution witnesses u/s. 161 Cr. P.C., the finding that the F.I.R. was not written at the place of occurrence as alleged by PW-18, the number of injuries on the deceased do not commensurate with the number of accused persons alleged to have assaulted the deceased, all taken together creates sufficient doubt in the prosecution case, and therefore, the accused persons are entitled to get the benefit of doubt.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has been able to prove the charges against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
The object of the unlawful assembly being to stop the laborers from transplanting paddy seeds on the field in question, the conviction under Section 302/149 cannot be upheld.
court_reasoning: The court scrutinized the evidence of the eye-witnesses and ultimately came to hold that prosecution case as unfolded through those witnesses implicating the accused persons in the commission of two murders must be held to have been established beyond reasonable doubt.
Apart from holding that the occular statement of the eye-witnesses corroborates each other, court also came to the conclusion that the medical evidence corroborates the prosecution case.

The High Court rejected the argument advanced on behalf of the accused persons that the prosecution party was the aggressor and came upon the field to dispossess one of the accused persons Sanjam Pandey.
holding: The conviction under Section 302/149 cannot be upheld, but as stated earlier the conviction on other counts was maintained.
